access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge renewed (Dec 2029) through 2031. Payment rises from $245 to $275/month to absorb the tariff and shortage repricing; the copay stays $50 and the criteria are unchanged, with a documented DEXA/strength counselling visit for 65+. About 2.3M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 2.3M × $275 × 12 ≈ $7.6B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈15.5% of incretin fills ≈ 7.8M users (7.4M adults 65+ plus ~0.4M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays ≈11% ≈ 5.5M users at $275: 5.5M × $275 × 12 ≈ $18.2B/yr combined federal and state. The Indiana and Arkansas adherence waivers are unchanged. The new HRSA Community Incretin Access Program is a grant programme, not insurance. It provides free generic liraglutide through FQHCs and free semaglutide for smoking cessation and AUD through state quitlines and SUD clinics, for ≈3.0M users: 2.0M liraglutide × $85 federal contract × 12 = $2.0B, plus 1.0M semaglutide × $199 × 12 = $2.4B, ≈ $4.4B/yr against a $4.5B FY2030 appropriation.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 70+ semaglutide brands at $8–45/month and the first generic tirzepatide filings. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and China sell generic semaglutide. Generic oral semaglutide is available in ~175 countries. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.

The ACA preventive mandate requires plans to cover FDA-approved cessation drugs, which now includes semaglutide, for two 90-day courses a year. Mental-health parity requires plans that exclude weight drugs to cover semaglutide for AUD on medical-equivalent terms. Prior-auth AUDIT scores have drifted upward, and plans call this 'indication shopping'. Gray prices: US 503A telehealth 'personalised' compounded semaglutide $129–249; Indian mail pens $8–45 plus shipping; 'research-use' retatrutide vials $120–250, with no prescriber.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached market (driver: none). Survodutide received an FDA complete response letter in Jan 2029 over hepatic-signal questions and manufacturing data; it has been resubmitted, with a decision not before 2031. Amycretin (NDA filed Jun 2028) received a CRL in Oct 2029 tied to the same Novo fill-finish facility findings behind the Wegovy recall; resubmission is pending. MariTide (monthly) phase 3 read out and its BLA was filed Jul 2030, so approval is no earlier than mid-2031. Bimagrumab combinations entered phase 3 in 2029 and are not on the market. The new indications come as supplements to existing drugs: semaglutide for smoking cessation (sNDA May 2028, approved Mar 2029) and AUD (sNDA Aug 2029, priority review, approved Jun 2030), and liraglutide for ages 6–11. The under-12 driver is realised through generic-eligible liraglutide, not newer agents. The incretin market is ≈$135B in 2030: US volume nearly doubled, and the tariff repricing offset ex-US generic erosion.

food_and_beverage.state: With nearly one adult in five on the drug, volume losses in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks are about double the 2026–28 rate. Majors cut US volume guidance and accelerate sales of indulgent brands. Protein, fibre and bone-health formats keep growing. Discount grocers report a split basket: more protein in affluent zip codes and less in subsidy-heavy ones.

alcohol.state: The AUD approval and parity coverage reach heavy drinkers, the category's profit core. US spirits volumes fall again and beer contracts. Premium 'one good drink' formats and non-alcoholic lines grow. Tobacco and vape makers report cessation-driven declines, which state excise forecasts now model.

restaurants.state: Fine dining and protein-forward fast casual are adapted and steady. Value-volume chains and buffets in mid-income suburbs close underperforming units. Alcohol attach rates fall across the sector.

apparel.state: Size runs keep widening as bodies move both ways. 'Athletic-cut' tailoring for lean, muscled affluent clients is the growth segment. Plus-size retailers shrink further as bottom-third uptake rises.

fitness.state: Strength-and-DEXA studios expand into second-tier metros. A gym-floor gray market in research-peptide retatrutide draws FDA letters. Low-cost gyms gain members from subsidy users.

insurance.state: The structure is unchanged, but pharmacy trend runs at ~+14% because the cessation mandate and AUD parity force coverage that weight-loss exclusions had blocked. Employer weight-management coverage drifts from 58% to 57%. Adherence gating spreads to cessation and AUD benefits.

pharma.state: Lilly is the volume and margin leader. Novo is recovering from the recall, the amycretin CRL and HELP findings. Both book MDL reserves in the low billions, and tariff repricing lifted US net prices. The generic liraglutide makers that won the HRSA contracts are the surprise winners.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The question is no longer whether someone is on the drug but what they are on and who pays. A lean, muscled, DEXA-tracked body reads as retatrutide plus a coach: top-third money. A thinner body without much muscle reads as kiosk-weigh-in Medicaid, free liraglutide or a compounded pen. A heavier body reads as uninsured, off on purpose, or between 90-day quit courses.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Thinness and muscle are class uniforms. In Charlotte's banking and fintech workforce, men aged 30–49 wear 'the Charlotte build': retatrutide on allocation through concierge practices, a strength coach and quarterly DEXA. Recruiters admit they notice it. Use in the bottom third doubled, mostly on lower-efficacy or unverified product, so the gap is now less about being on or off and more about the quality of the result.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals are smaller across many households. Children on liraglutide at the family table have made 'kid portions' a family-doctor topic. Weddings serve two menus. Bars and tasting rooms sell experiences more than volume.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles state the molecule as well as on or off. 'Reta' signals money, and 'clinic pen' is a mild put-down. Mismatched appetites in mixed couples remain openly discussed.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite of every kind is treated as a clinical variable. Since the AUD and cessation approvals, a craving left untreated is read as a choice, and in some workplaces as a liability.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Reduced-pleasure reports hold at ~10–15% of long-term users, dose-dependent. Interim retatrutide anhedonia-scale data are ambiguous. At least a dozen telehealth brands now sell low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo subscriptions ($199–279/month) to people without obesity, explicitly for 'quiet', 'focus' and 'freedom from craving'. An estimated 1.5–2M adults use them, counted inside the cash and gray shares.
interior_life.framing: Sold as a feature. Wellness brands advertise 'the off switch for noise'. Clinicians still say 'dose-dependent reward modulation'. Users who dislike the effect call it 'the grey' and lower their dose. Regulators treat it as advertising, not pharmacology.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers have moved from rewarding observable correlates to subsidising 'focus' subscriptions as a perk in finance, call centres and logistics. Trucking fleets still rely on tirzepatide for DOT apnea clearance. Sales and creative staff still go off-dose before pitches. Unions in three national contracts won language barring employers from viewing PBM adherence data.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Writing off-dose' has become a credited aesthetic: a touring circuit, small-label albums and comedy specials billed as unmedicated. Leisure keeps shifting toward intense, short experiences such as sauna, cold plunge and single tastings. Sports betting operators report softer handle in high-uptake states and say so on earnings calls.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists routinely ask about dose. Couples on 'focus' subscriptions report fewer fights and less wanting, and describe both as true. Dose holidays around anniversaries are a commonplace joke.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Visible on price, tariffs, free provision and torts. Talk-radio hosts on both sides call the HRSA programme 'pacification pills', but no turnout or mood effect is measured. Candidates are asked whether they are 'on'.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on indications (cessation, AUD, ages 6–11) and still defensive on safety: CRLs for survodutide and amycretin, Novo facility enforcement, HELP findings. Gray-market enforcement is selective and largely symbolic once shortage-exception compounding ended. The FTC, not the FDA, polices 'calm/focus' marketing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy: the HRSA Community Incretin Access Program was funded through a bipartisan appropriations rider (Jul 2029, $4.5B for FY2030) and provides free generic liraglutide at FQHCs and free semaglutide through quitlines and SUD clinics. It is discretionary and must be renewed annually. There is no mandate to take the drug. The Medicare Bridge was renewed at $275/$50, and the ACA cessation mandate and parity law now apply to semaglutide.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged: ≥80% PDC and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses. Three more states have applied. HRSA programme sites require only refill pickup, not weigh-ins. That creates a two-tier conditioning system, which waiver plaintiffs cite.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT apnea screening still makes tirzepatide a de facto requirement for some drivers. The Army keeps its contested recruit policy. The VA adopted semaglutide for AUD under the 2029 VA/DoD guideline.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 tariff final rule (Jan 2029) and Novo's US plant failure repriced the branded supply. India's mail-order exports to the US are a standing item in trade talks. Indian API also feeds US 503A compounders, so tariff policy and gray-market supply are tied together.

events.event: FDA warning letter and lot recall at Novo Nordisk's North Carolina fill-finish site put semaglutide injection on the shortage list; days later the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff final rule takes effect, and TrumpRx cash prices rise to $349 (semaglutide) and $449 (tirzepatide), with oral starting doses at $199
FDA extends liraglutide's obesity indication, including generic versions, to children aged 6–11, requiring a pediatric registry and a bone-accrual study

Bipartisan appropriations rider funds a $4.5B HRSA Community Incretin Access Program: free generic liraglutide at community health centres and free semaglutide for smoking cessation and alcohol treatment through state quitlines and SUD clinics

FDA removes semaglutide from the shortage list, ending legal shortage-exception compounding, but telehealth 'personalised dose' 503A sellers and 'research-use' retatrutide vendors keep shipping; FDA sends ~40 warning letters as an estimated 9M Americans use gray-market product
First bellwether verdict in MDL 3094 finds for a plaintiff with persistent gastroparesis; filed and tolled GI and pancreatitis claims pass 40,000 and both manufacturers book litigation reserves

open_tensions: Free provision, the cessation mandate and AUD parity doubled use among lower-income Americans, mostly on lower-efficacy or unverified product with no body-composition monitoring, while the affluent pay for retatrutide plus a coach. The state is subsidising exactly the regimen the bone and muscle labels warn about.
The gray market is now 18% of users and is fed by the same Indian API the tariff was meant to price out. Enforcement against it would collide with a subsidy programme whose purpose is access.

Reward blunting is sold as a feature, subsidised as an employee perk and approved as a treatment for alcohol and nicotine, but has still not been measured as a harm. The first validated anhedonia data from retatrutide postmarketing studies are due in 2031.
Mass-tort claims are moving ahead of causal evidence on pancreatitis and persistent gastroparesis. Settlement pressure may reshape labels and prices before the science settles.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity runs to ~2031–32.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Retatrutide still lists at $1,499 a month, is supply-allocated, has no TrumpRx cash price, and carries its bone and body-composition monitoring section.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: Free Pills for the Poor, Retatrutide for the Rich: One in Five Americans Is On It, and You Can Tell Who Paid
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030 nearly one American adult in five is on an incretin drug, about fifty million people, close to twice the number two years ago. This happened while the price went up. In January 2029 an FDA warning letter shut lines at Novo Nordisk's North Carolina fill-finish plant, semaglutide went onto the shortage list, and the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff took effect in the same month. The cash portal raised semaglutide to $349 a month, tirzepatide to $449 and the starter pill to $199. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349, and retatrutide is still $1,499 and rationed.

Three channels carried people past the price. The first was existing law. Semaglutide's smoking-cessation approval in 2029 brought it under the ACA's preventive mandate, and its alcohol-use-disorder approval in June 2030 brought it under mental-health parity. Plans that had refused to pay for weight loss now pay for quitting and for drinking less, two ninety-day courses at a time. Benefits managers watch AUDIT scores creep upward and call it indication shopping.

The second was the state. A bipartisan appropriations rider funded a $4.5 billion federal programme that hands out generic liraglutide free at community health centres and free semaglutide through quitlines and addiction clinics, about three million people in all. Liraglutide is older, daily and weaker, but it is generic and now labelled for children from six. About ninety thousand children under twelve are on a drug, and no one has bone data for them.

The third was the gray market. The shortage briefly made compounding legal again. When it ended, the telehealth pharmacies kept shipping 'personalised doses', gyms began selling vials of retatrutide labelled for research, and Indian pens kept arriving by mail. About nine million Americans use product no American regulator has inspected. The FDA sends letters. Poison-centre calls have doubled.

The result is a country where nearly everyone can get some version of the drug, but the versions differ. In Charlotte's banks, men in their thirties and forties have the same build: retatrutide through a concierge practice, a strength coach, a DEXA scan every quarter. Recruiters notice it, and so does everyone else. Bottom-third use has doubled to thirteen percent, mostly on liraglutide, rationed courses or a compounded pen, and often without muscle monitoring. Thin no longer marks the line between classes. The finish does: muscle, bone and a measured dose. In Gary, Indiana, the Medicaid weigh-in kiosk still decides who keeps coverage. The free clinic down the street asks for nothing but a refill pickup, and the waiver plaintiffs have noticed.

The quieting effect that people named the Ozempic personality in 2026 has become a product. A dozen wellness brands sell low-dose pill subscriptions for 'quiet' and 'freedom from craving' to people who were never heavy, and some employers now pay for them as a perk. The FTC has sent warning letters. Surveys still find that one long-term user in eight feels less pleasure. Musicians bill their tours as off-dose. Sports-betting companies blame softer betting volume on their customers' medication.

The lawsuits arrived with the volume. More than forty thousand gastroparesis and pancreatitis claims sit in a federal courtroom in Philadelphia. A jury found for the first bellwether plaintiff in March. The pancreatitis science still says 'suspected', and the claims keep coming anyway. Spirits makers cut guidance again. Snack makers sell indulgent brands. Both drugmakers report record US revenue. From a distance the country looks calmer and leaner, and it drinks less. Up close, you can tell from someone's body who paid for their drug.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tasha Greer weighs herself on the bathroom scale at 5:40, though nothing rides on that one anymore. She missed two kiosk weigh-ins last winter while working doubles, and Indiana locked her out of Medicaid coverage until March. Her pen comes from a telehealth pharmacy in Florida: $179, a vial, a box of syringes and a dosing card she keeps on the fridge next to Jaylen's spelling list.

Jaylen is nine. His liraglutide is free from the health centre on Broadway, and they never ask him to step on anything. She does his shot at the counter while he eats half a waffle. He says it pinches. She says everything pinches.

By eight she's in Crown Point at Mr. Albrecht's, a retired bank man with a stoop that his coach says is improving. His retatrutide comes in a cooler bag from a concierge doctor. She lays out his protein shake, his calcium and his DEXA printout for Thursday, and helps him through twelve slow squats holding the kitchen counter. He tells her she looks good, lighter. She says thank you and doesn't say what she pays.

At lunch her sister texts a link from a law firm, Stomach problems after Ozempic? Tasha's stomach is fine. She deletes it.

After pickup, Jaylen wants McDonald's and finishes four nuggets before he stops, folds the box and says he's done. She eats his fries without wanting them, out of habit.

At nine she sets the pen supplies out for Sunday and checks the date on the dosing card. She writes 'March' on the calendar in red, then 'kiosk' under it, twice.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class or indication reached market this step. The semaglutide smoking-cessation sNDA received a CRL (Mar 2029) asking for validated neuropsychiatric and anhedonia endpoints; Novo plans a new trial and does not expect resubmission before 2031. food_and_beverage.state: With current use up to 14.6%, volume pressure resumes in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks: US salty-snack volume is down ~2–3% a year in 2029–30, against roughly flat before. Protein, fibre, calcium and vitamin D claims are standard. 'Bone-forward' dairy and fortified foods are the fastest-growing lines. A small countertrend of 'real food, full portion' heritage brands courts the backlash audience. Major packaged-food firms keep trimming SKUs rather than exiting categories.

alcohol.state: Contracting again. Heavy-drinker volumes keep falling, and 'calm' subscriptions take a slice of occasional drinkers who used alcohol to unwind. Spirits majors report a third straight year of US volume decline. On-premise 'one good drink' formats hold. Tobacco and vape makers report accelerating quit rates in investor calls despite the smoking-cessation CRL.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat, and spend per cover is down in high-uptake suburbs. Half portions, protein bowls priced by the gram, and 'on/off' menus are standard. Buffets and value-volume casual chains keep closing units. A handful of soul-food and Southern-comfort independents in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston market themselves explicitly as 'no-gram' rooms and are doing well.

apparel.state: Size churn is the business model. Cycling users and DEXA-advised pauses keep sizes moving both ways. Plus-size specialists are stable and lean into the body-sovereignty revival with campaigns and models who are off the drug by choice.

fitness.state: Growing on the bone wave. 'Prescribed lifting', DEXA-plus-coaching chains and Medicare Advantage strength benefits are now mainstream. Several MA plans make strength-class attendance a soft condition of GLP-1 prior authorisation. Some markets have DEXA capacity shortages, and mobile DEXA vans serve suburban gyms.

insurance.state: Employer coverage rose from 58% to 63% because lower net prices (≈$170–190) plus outcome gating made the benefit budgetable. About 70% of covering employers gate, which shifts cost onto non-responders and non-adherers, who lose coverage. BMI-linked surcharges are widespread. Pharmacy trend has eased to ~+6% as price cuts offset volume. Bone-related claims (DEXA, antiresorptives, fracture care) are a new line in GLP-1 cost models.

pharma.state: Lilly dominates US volume through tirzepatide, retatrutide and Foundayo. Novo is weakened, with the HELP report, DOJ exposure and generic erosion abroad, but holds Medicare share through semaglutide. US net prices are down ~15–20% while US volume is up ~45%. Bone-agent makers and DEXA equipment suppliers are surprise winners. Brand-protection and pen-authentication technology is a growth niche.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among insured professionals, being on the drug is still the default. 'Off' now has two respectable readings, medical ('my DEXA') and principled ('I came off on purpose'), alongside the old ones of lapsed coverage or discipline. Visible regain in a gated plan is read as having been cut off. The 'on it too long' look of thin arms and a forward stoop is recognised in people over 55, and resistance-trained shoulders are the new marker of doing it right.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The gradient narrowed slightly in level but widened in quality. The top third (18.5%) runs low-dose or retatrutide regimens with DEXA, coaching and antiresorptives when needed. The bottom third (10.3%) gets there through Medicaid at $199, gated employer plans, or Indian and Chinese pens bought by mail with no scan at all. In counterfeit-cluster cities (Houston, Phoenix, Miami) people ask whether the pen is 'real' before they ask what dose.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are smaller and protein-first. Counter to that, 'full-table' Sunday dinners, church potlucks and 'no-gram' restaurants are defended as heritage. Holiday hosting now plans for three groups: on, off, and off-by-conviction.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles state on/off. Some backlash communities add 'unmedicated' as an identity filter. 'Calm' subscribers describe partners finding them easier and also less fun, and the mismatch is a staple of advice columns.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is medicalised and is now also politicised as a counterclaim. The backlash has three strands. A fat-acceptance and body-sovereignty revival is led by Black women's wellness collectives in Atlanta. A religious 'appetite is a gift' framing comes from Southern Baptist and Pentecostal congregations in the Tulsa–Dallas corridor. A 'natural metabolic' supplement market (berberine, 'nature's GLP-1' fibres) is allied to anti-pharma influencers. These strands agree on little except refusing the drug, and the counterfeit deaths and bone data fuel all three.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Interim postmarketing SHAPS data show clinically meaningful anhedonia increases in ~10–14% of top-dose retatrutide users versus ~5% of comparators; the data are dose-dependent and observational. Among an estimated ~1.5–2M Americans on low-dose 'calm' or 'craving freedom' subscriptions, there is no systematic measurement. Subscriber surveys run by the vendors report high satisfaction, which says little.
interior_life.framing: Sold as a feature. Telehealth wellness brands sell 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked' subscriptions (low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo, $149–199/month cash) with copy about calm, focus, and freedom from 'noise' (snacking, scrolling, a second glass). Clinicians still say 'dose-dependent reward modulation'. Complaining users call it 'the grey', and the FTC calls some of the claims unsubstantiated.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Gated plans link adherence to employment-tied coverage. PBM dashboards show employers enrolment and outcome tiers, though not individual data in unionised shops after 2029 Teamster and SEIU contract language. Fleets and call centres favour staying on. Tech and finance firms reimburse 'focus' subscriptions through lifestyle-spending accounts, which lets the product reach people without obesity. In sales, creative and hospitality jobs, workers quietly cut doses before pitches and service peaks.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' is an aesthetic claim. A Nashville songwriting scene and several touring comics advertise sets as written unmedicated, and backlash audiences reward it. Users keep seeking intense stimulus: hot sauce, loud venues and extreme sports bookings are up among subscribers. Fan communities argue about whether a beloved artist's flatter new album is 'the grey'.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose and for 'calm' subscriptions. Some couples on the subscriptions report fewer fights and less desire. Dose-holiday weekends are an established practice, and backlash groups frame the drugs as a threat to marriage and fertility.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Still mainly about cost, control and safety. The counterfeit deaths and the India and China price gap are both stump material, used both for 'let us import legally' and for 'seal the mail'. Body-sovereignty and religious-natural groups have joined disability advocates against gating, which is an odd coalition. There are no established turnout or temperament effects, though campaign consultants test 'calm voter' messaging and do not publish the results.

state.regulatory_posture: There is no new state action this window, only continuation. The FDA is slow and data-demanding on new filings (CRLs for smoking cessation and survodutide, an extended amycretin review) because of the bone wave. Enforcement against imports remains selective: import alerts, warnings and seizures. Individuals are not prosecuted and Congress has passed no new importation law. The FTC acts on advertising claims only.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. The federal direct-pricing portal and the Medicare Bridge successor carry the managed decline: $199 injectables, $149–199 orals, and $199 Medicare/Medicaid rate with a $50 Medicare copay. Medicaid coverage remains state by state.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Existing conditioning continues unchanged: the Indiana and Arkansas 1115 waivers (≥80% PDC, quarterly verified weigh-ins, two misses = 12 months off) and wellness rules allowing BMI-linked surcharges up to 30% of premium. Most of the growth in conditioning is private: ~70% of covering employers now gate through PBMs, including a ≥5% response threshold. Weigh-in kiosk networks in pharmacy chains now serve both Medicaid and commercial plans.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still makes tirzepatide a de facto job requirement for some drivers. Army accession policy on GLP-1 use is unchanged and still contested. Some fleets now add DEXA screening for drivers over 55 after injury claims.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: China joins India as the visible source of cheap supply. Chinese API underlies much of the gray trade and is implicated in contaminated vials, which turns a price story into a security story in congressional rhetoric. India–US trade talks treat mail-order pharma as a bargaining item. Section 232 tariffs remain, and the Dec 2029 price deal was framed as manufacturers absorbing some tariff cost in exchange for domestic-capacity credits.

open_tensions: Private gating now covers most insured users and rewards continuous use and steady loss, while the 2029–30 bone guidance recommends DEXA-driven pauses. A medically advised pause can trip the adherence rule and cost a worker their coverage for a year.

About 3M Americans use imported or counterfeit product. Counterfeit deaths and Chinese-sourced contamination push toward sealing the mail, while $5–30 generics abroad and the coming 2031–32 US exclusivity cliff push toward legal importation. Neither has been legislated.

Reward blunting is now a retail product sold to people without obesity, through employer accounts and outside any indication, while the only near-RCT-grade data call it a dose-dependent harm in up to one in seven top-dose users.

The backlash coalition of fat acceptance, religious 'natural' framings, anti-pharma supplement sellers and disability advocates agrees only on opposing gating. It is now large enough that candidates court it, and it has no shared position on whether the drugs should be cheaper.

prose.headline: The Quiet Country: 39 million Americans are on the drug, their bones are thinning, and a fake pen can kill you
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about one American adult in seven is on an incretin drug, up from one in ten two years ago. The rise did not come from a miracle molecule. No new class reached the market, and the FDA, unsettled by the bone data, spent the window sending sponsors back for scans. It came from arithmetic and paperwork. In December 2029 the government and the two manufacturers agreed a step-down: weekly injectables at $199 on the federal direct portal, higher oral doses at $199, and a Medicare rate of $199 from January with the same $50 copay. Pharmacy-benefit managers had already done their own deal. Employers could buy coverage at under $200 a month net, provided members stayed adherent, stepped on a verified scale, and lost at least five percent by month six. Coverage became affordable because it became conditional, and nearly two-thirds of employers now offer it.

Most of the new users are not first-timers. More than four in ten people who have ever taken these drugs have stopped and started again. Cheaper prices made restarting easy, and so did a parcel from Hyderabad or Shenzhen. About three million Americans now inject product no American prescriber has seen. In August 2029 pens sold as Ozempic through social-media shops turned out to contain insulin. Four people died and about a hundred and sixty went to emergency rooms in Texas, Florida and Arizona. Poison-centre calls have doubled. The FDA posted pictures showing how to tell a real pen from a fake. Congress has held hearings but passed nothing, and the people buying cheap pens keep buying them.

The bones are the slow story. By 2030 a second large cohort has confirmed what the first suggested: older long-term users break hips and vertebrae about a third more often. It adds something new, a smaller excess among women in their fifties who have cycled on and off several times. That works out to roughly five thousand extra hip fractures a year in a country that has three hundred thousand. Endocrinologists now order DEXA scans the way they once ordered lipid panels. In some cities the wait for a scan runs to three months, and mobile scanners park outside suburban gyms. Strength classes are a condition of some Medicare Advantage approvals. Generic zoledronic acid has become a companion prescription.

The drugs' quieting effect has been put on sale. The FDA declined to approve semaglutide for smoking, saying no one had properly measured what it does to pleasure. Telehealth brands market the same effect anyway, as 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked': low-dose pills at $149 a month for calm, focus and freedom from craving, sold to people who were never heavy and sometimes reimbursed by tech employers as a lifestyle perk. The FTC has sent warning letters. Early postmarketing data on retatrutide suggest that at top doses roughly one user in eight or nine reports a meaningful loss of pleasure. Users call it 'the grey'.

Against all this a counter-movement has formed, and its members disagree with each other. Black women's wellness collectives in Atlanta revived fat acceptance as body sovereignty. Baptist and Pentecostal congregations from Tulsa to Dallas preach appetite as a gift. Supplement influencers sell berberine as nature's version. Fracture plaintiffs and disability advocates bring the lawsuits. In April they marched together against gated coverage. 'Unmedicated' has become a dating filter and a selling point for songwriters.

On the surface things look orderly. Snack volumes are slipping again, spirits are falling for a third year, and gyms are full of sixty-year-olds deadlifting. Underneath, the institutions that pay for the drug reward people for never stopping, while the doctors reading the new bone guidance increasingly tell them to stop.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Watkins, 58, is up at five because the Walgreens on Broadway opens its kiosk at six and her shift starts at seven. She takes off her shoes, steps on, and looks into the little camera. The screen says VERIFIED and prints a receipt. She photographs the receipt anyway.

She drives to Mr. Hollins, who is ninety-one and can't get out of his recliner alone. She lifts him under the arms. Her own wrist aches when she does it, and that was the reason for the scan in March. The clinic letter is on her fridge with the word osteopenia circled in a nurse's blue pen. Pause for six months, the doctor said, then rescan. Denise asked what happens to her coverage if she pauses. The doctor said she'd write a letter. Denise has not heard back about the letter.

At lunch her sister texts a link: forty dollars, three pens, shipped from India. Underneath it she's put a photo of the CDC warning, with a question mark.

At Mr. Hollins's she eats half a turkey wrap and gives him the other half.

In the evening the church basement smells like greens and cornbread. Pastor Ellis calls it Whole Table Wednesday. Denise sits with a plate she won't finish while a woman from Merrillville talks about her hip, her husband, and the year she lost to the scale. People nod.

At home she takes the pen out of the fridge and holds it, cold, for a while. Then she puts it back on the shelf behind the eggs, next to the letter.

indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Jun 2029, on SCALE Kids)

reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial ongoing). An sNDA to extend it to adults 60+ with obesity without CVD was accepted Sep 2030, with a decision in 2031
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction via telehealth and employer EAPs (oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 reads out 2031)
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, cash-paid on orals or tirzepatide

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Retatrutide had been under review since Feb 2027 (decision extended). It was approved Mar 2029 with dysesthesia labelling and a top dose limited to 9 mg for most patients; labelled efficacy is ~24%. Survodutide (filed Jun 2028) was approved Aug 2029, with uptake mostly in MASH. The monthly-injection driver is realised by MariTide. It was in phase 3 (MARITIME programme) at the start of the step with no filing stated. Amgen filed the BLA in Mar 2029 and the FDA approved it in Apr 2030, 13 months later, at ~17% weight loss with more early vomiting than the weekly drugs. No implant exists; implant programmes remain preclinical or phase 1. Amycretin was filed in Oct 2029, so no decision is due before late 2030 and it is not approved. No oral matches tirzepatide. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts are still in phase 3 and not approved. The pediatric under-12 approval is an existing product in a new population (liraglutide, daily injection). The cognition driver is realised through expanded Part D use of the existing tirzepatide label and a newly filed sNDA, not a new approval. Global incretin market ~$140B (2029). US net prices are drifting down a few percent a year.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. MariTide's early vomiting is higher than the weekly drugs'. Chronic diarrhoea in long-term users is now being re-examined in light of the exocrine pancreatic signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. The new exocrine signal reopened the litigation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL settlements finalised 2029, and new filings now cite exocrine insufficiency.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Follow-up of the Medicare cohort holds the hip-fracture HR at ~1.3 in users 65+ after >2 years. Risk is higher (~1.45) among people who have cycled three or more times. Dementia-route patients, the oldest users, carry the highest absolute fracture risk. Retatrutide's larger loss raises lean-mass concern.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained, and DXA code in use. Retatrutide label adds a resistance-training and protein counselling statement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning remains removed.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A 2029 replication cohort (n≈31k) puts clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls. It is dose-related, and retatrutide users show the highest rates (~10%). No randomised data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA postmarketing observational study under way; no labelling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Gray-market users who quit after bad batches regain fastest.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency now consistently documented in low-intake users. Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency is linked to the exocrine signal in long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance recommends annual micronutrient panels; label language under FDA review.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Danish national registries hold the longest high-dose semaglutide exposure. A Feb 2030 registry study, replicated in a US Optum cohort in May 2030, found new EPI diagnoses (low faecal elastase, steatorrhoea) at ~4.1 per 1,000 person-years in users continuously on drug for more than 5 years, against ~1.9 in matched controls with similar weight loss. There was no excess before year 4. Imaging substudies suggest reduced pancreatic volume. It was missed for years because chronic loose stools were attributed to known GI effects. The signal compounds the bone problem through vitamin D and K malabsorption. It is unknown whether it reverses on stopping or extends to tirzepatide at the same rate (tirzepatide exposure beyond 5 years is still thin).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Jun 2030) advises faecal elastase testing for long-term users with persistent diarrhoea or weight-independent nutritional decline. EMA PRAC review opened. Class labelling not yet decided.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up now exist for semaglutide, and the first true long-horizon signal (EPI) appeared there. The under-12 approval extends potential lifetime exposure to 60+ years. Pediatric bone data are not yet reported.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone-density and growth postmarketing requirements attached to the 2029 liraglutide 6–11 approval.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~14,000 by mid-2030. In Sep 2029 counterfeit 'Ozempic' pens containing insulin caused 112 hospitalisations for severe hypoglycaemia and 4 deaths across 9 states. 'Research-grade' retatrutide sold before approval and fake 'monthly' vials led to overdose presentations. Poison-centre calls are ~4× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert expanded to finished pens. CBP seizures roughly doubled. Lilly and Novo serialised pens with scannable authentication. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

food_and_beverage.state: About 33% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~7–9% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~7%. Dollar sales are flat to slightly down. The aisle has split by class: premium protein, fibre and 'lean-mass' lines sell in upper-income suburbs, while value packs and private label hold in lower-income zip codes where use is lower and regain is common. Hershey and Mondelez keep trimming SKUs. Protein ingredients (whey, pea) are in shortage pricing.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~10% from 2025 and beer ~6%. Heavy-drinker demand keeps eroding through EAP-driven off-label use. Brown-Forman and Diageo have consolidated more US capacity. Non-alcoholic lines are growing but do not replace the lost margin. Bar closures are concentrated in mid-sized Midwestern cities.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Checks are smaller at casual dining. Small-plate and protein menus are standard. Buffets keep closing. Fast-casual 'macro bowls' priced for the upper tier sit alongside value-menu growth at QSRs in lower-income markets.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep contracting (Torrid down roughly 40% in stores from 2024). Growth is in premium fitted and athletic 'structured' wear for lifted, lean bodies. Stretch, resale and rental serve cyclers. Sizing has bifurcated by retailer price point.

fitness.state: Strength training and body-composition scanning keep growing. Premium clubs sell DXA-plus-coaching memberships at $250–400 a month. Budget gyms have converted cardio floors to racks. Employer metabolic tracks now bundle monthly-injection clinic visits with check-ins.

insurance.state: Employer coverage for weight management is down to 36%. Pharmacy trend ~+7% in 2030 as flat-net PBM deals offset volume. Coverage sits on diabetes, cardiac, OSA and dementia codes behind prior authorisation. Wellness differentials tied to adherence have spread to more mid-sized self-insured firms, and clinic-administered monthly dosing makes verification trivial. Medicare Part D plans are raising premiums partly on incretin spend.

pharma.state: Lilly and Novo still dominate, now joined by Amgen (MariTide) and Boehringer (survodutide). US net prices are drifting down through TrumpRx and PBM deals but hold above $150. Lilly's retatrutide and dementia franchise lead growth. Novo leans on the oral and the Medicare negotiated price. Counterfeit protection (serialisation, litigation) is a nine-figure cost line. Indian and Chinese generic makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body shape now reads mostly as income. A lean body with visible muscle and good skin reads as covered, scanned and coached, which means upper tier. A lean, soft, slightly depleted body reads as cash or mail-order. A regained body over 50 reads as lost coverage. 'Lifted' has replaced 'thin' as the marker of the top tier.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class uniform is muscle. In Charlotte's banking and Austin's tech offices, DXA printouts are shared like marathon times, and lean-mass percentage is gossip. In Columbus-area logistics, a monthly shot at the on-site clinic is part of the job, and the body that results is thin without the muscle. Among bottom-third women aged 50–64, the most visible group is the regainers: they were on the drug through the Bridge pilot or through jobs they no longer have. Upper-income children under 12 are now a medicated cohort as well.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter. Protein has become a manners question (what you serve signals whether you understand your guests). The 'Bread Alone' church fasting network claims ~500 congregations, strongest in Oklahoma and Arkansas, and frames unmedicated fasting as a discipline the poor can afford. School lunch debates now include children on daily liraglutide.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added 'lean-mass verified' badges through scan-chain partnerships, a premium-tier feature. 'On' and 'off' markers persist. Desire mismatch remains a common therapy complaint, and couples now negotiate around the monthly shot date instead of weekly.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Upper-tier culture treats appetite as noise that has been managed. In lower-income communities appetite is either a sign of lost access or a point of pride. The counter-movement (Unmuted, fat-acceptance revivalists, MAHA-adjacent influencers, fasting churches) has grown but split further. Unmuted now argues explicitly about class, while the MAHA wing argues about pharma.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, up to ~10% on retatrutide. A much larger share report mild 'evenness', and employers prize it.
interior_life.framing: HR calls it 'steadiness' and now writes it into competency language ('even under pressure'). Clinicians call it a dose-related side effect. Unmuted calls it a class sedative: the pay grades that most need patience are the ones medicated into it.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 4.5M employees are in adherence-verified tracks, and monthly clinic-administered MariTide removes the self-report step entirely. Logistics firms in the Columbus corridor, national call-centre operators and state employee plans in Texas and Indiana report adherence alongside safety and attendance metrics. Shift-lead promotions informally favour enrollees. The two EEOC ADA charges are still pending, unresolved after two years. Managers in upper-tier firms do not monitor anything; their staff pay cash or use rich plans and are trusted.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Unmuted 'off nights' have spread to Detroit and Baltimore and now draw explicitly working-class crowds. 'Flat' fiction has a commercial imprint. Sportsbooks' wagering per active account is down, with the drop concentrated in insured suburbs. Loud, sour, spicy food and music remain a genre. Late-night bar culture keeps contracting in mid-sized cities.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: The monthly shot date replaced weekly timing as the thing couples plan around. Drug holidays around anniversaries persist but are harder on a monthly product, so some couples simply live with mismatch. Therapists report fewer 'holiday' cycles and more 'parallel lives'.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The left–right coalition against adherence-conditioned premiums stalled. California's bill died in appropriations, and no new state laws passed in the window. The movement now speaks about class more than mood. 'Sedated electorate' claims still have no turnout evidence. The visible political fact is that the medicated and the regained increasingly vote in different zip codes.

state.regulatory_posture: No new state action. The FDA continues its pro-speed posture on routine approvals (retatrutide, survodutide, MariTide, pediatric liraglutide) and issued a drug safety communication on the exocrine signal. The rhetoric on imports is unchanged and enforcement is still porous. Neither Congress nor HHS created new coverage, mandates or premium rules in the window.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx operates on manufacturer-set prices. The Medicare Bridge pilot was not revived. The 2027 tri-agency 30% wellness guidance stands unchanged.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law, deeper in practice. PBM fill data, app logs and now clinic administration records for monthly injections flow to wellness vendors under consent forms. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules are unchanged. The Army recruit oral pilot continues without expansion. DOT still has not ruled on off-label alcohol-reduction use among drivers.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply most of the world's incretin volume. US–India trade talks keep CBP mail enforcement on the agenda without an agreement. Danish and US politicians still spar over the price gap, now ~40× between Indian generics and US cash prices.

events.event: FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide for obesity after a two-year review, with dysesthesia labelling and a lean-mass counselling statement; Lilly prices it at a $1,299 list and steers it to commercial formularies

Novo and Lilly cut TrumpRx maintenance prices (Wegovy pill $249, injectables $279–349) and sign flat-net PBM deals; months later Business Group on Health finds only 36% of employers still cover weight loss
FDA approves liraglutide, including generics, for obesity in children aged 6–11 on SCALE Kids data, with bone-density and growth postmarketing requirements
CDC links counterfeit 'Ozempic' pens containing insulin to 112 hypoglycaemia hospitalisations and 4 deaths in 9 states; FDA expands import alert to finished pens
FDA approves Amgen's MariTide, the first monthly incretin injection, 13 months after filing; large employers move metabolic-track enrollees to clinic-administered monthly doses

FDA safety communication cites Danish and US cohorts showing doubled exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide; Lilly's sNDA to extend tirzepatide's dementia claim to people without heart disease is accepted in September

open_tensions: The longest-exposed users are the first to show the exocrine signal. Dementia prevention, adherence-conditioned premiums and pediatric use all assume decades of continuous therapy, the exposure the new signal says is not understood, and the FDA has not decided on class labelling.

Monthly clinic-administered dosing makes adherence verification trivial just as employer coverage contracts. Steadiness is becoming a condition of the jobs that still offer coverage, while the EEOC charges sit unresolved.
Five million Americans take mail-order or counterfeit product because US cash prices run ~40× India's, and each bad batch pushes the poorest users into abrupt discontinuation and regain.

Lilly's pending sNDA would open dementia-risk use to millions of older adults without heart disease, the group most exposed to the fracture warning, and Part D premiums are already rising on incretin spend.

prose.headline: The Monthly Body: In 2030 You Can Read a Paycheck in a Silhouette
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 a little under one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, and a quarter have tried one. The number rose slowly. What changed faster was who pays and what the result looks like. Employers kept leaving. Barely a third still cover the drugs for weight loss, and most of those that stay route patients through codes for diabetes, heart disease and, increasingly, dementia risk. Prices fell, but only as far as the manufacturers chose. Maintenance doses through the government's cash channel dropped to around $249 a month in 2029. Starting pills are still $149. The $1,349 list price is still on the box.

The new drugs arrived on schedule. Lilly's retatrutide, after a long review, takes off nearly a quarter of body weight and warns of strange skin sensations. Boehringer's survodutide found a home in liver clinics. In April, Amgen's MariTide became the first monthly shot. That mattered less for the chemistry than for the calendar. Large employers running monitored 'metabolic tracks' moved their enrollees to monthly doses given at on-site clinics, and adherence became a record kept by the clinic rather than something the employee reported. Around four and a half million workers now sit in those programmes, in warehouses outside Columbus, in call centres and in Texas and Indiana state offices. HR materials call the result steadiness. A replicated cohort says about one user in thirteen loses a clinically meaningful share of pleasure. Few people who sign the consent form read that far.

Children arrived too. Since June 2029 the old daily drug liraglutide, now generic, is approved for obesity from age six. A few hundred thousand children take it, most of them in households with good insurance and a pediatric endocrinologist, under postmarketing rules that will report on their bones in years, not months.

The most unsettling news came from Denmark, where people have taken high-dose semaglutide longest. A registry study in February, confirmed in American claims data by May, found that after five years of continuous use, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency roughly doubles: the pancreas stops making enough digestive enzymes. For years it had hidden inside the drug's ordinary diarrhoea. It also drains the vitamins that bones need, in the same population that already carries a hip-fracture warning. The FDA told doctors to test. It has not yet decided what the label should say. In September it accepted Lilly's request to extend the dementia-prevention claim to older adults without heart disease. The medicine is meant to be taken for decades, and the first decade-scale finding is now on record.

Below the insured tier, the mail runs heavier than before. About five million people take Indian vials, counterfeit pens or 'research' peptides bought through social shops. In September 2029, pens sold as Ozempic turned out to hold insulin, and four people died. The import alert was widened and the packages kept arriving.

In the shops and on the street, the consequence is a sorting of bodies. In Charlotte and Austin, the expensive body is lean and lifted, scanned twice a year and fed whey. On the logistics corridor it is thin and soft, and it belongs to someone with a monthly appointment at the plant clinic. In lower-income neighbourhoods the visible bodies are the regainers, people whose coverage or job ended. Snack makers sell premium protein in one zip code and value packs in another. Squat racks have replaced treadmills, and premium clubs charge $300 a month for scans and coaching.

No legislature intervened. California's premium bill died, the EEOC complaints sit undecided, and the coalition of churches, artists and MAHA legislators argues more about class now than about mood. Seen from a distance, the country is a little thinner and calmer.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tonya Mercer clocks in at the Groveport distribution centre at 5:40 a.m. She stops at the clinic trailer by the dock doors first, because the first Tuesday of the month is her shot. The nurse scans her badge, then the MariTide syringe, then her belly. The tablet chimes green. Her premium stays at the track rate for another month.

On the floor she runs a shift of thirty pickers. A new kid swears at a jammed conveyor and she waits it out without saying anything, which her review calls composure. She ate half a protein bar at nine and has not thought about food since.

At lunch she texts her sister Renée in Dayton, who buys Indian vials off a woman at church for twenty dollars. Renée sends a photo of the box. Tonya zooms in on the lot number and checks it against the recall list she keeps bookmarked. It isn't on it.

After shift she picks up her grandson Malik, nine, from school. He has a sticker on his backpack from the endocrinologist's office. Her daughter's insurance approved the generic liraglutide in March, and he does his own injection at the kitchen counter now. Every night he asks her if it pinches when she does hers. She tells him no.

At Kroger she walks past the dollar-bag chips without slowing down. A woman her age at the register is buying the big bag. Tonya remembers being that size two years ago, before this job.

At home she reads the pharmacy leaflet that came in the mail, about pancreas tests for people on these drugs five years or more. She has been on them three. She puts it on the fridge under a magnet.
